newsitem.title: USA: Simpson jury ends first full day without verdict.
newsitem.headline: Simpson jury ends first full day without verdict.

text.p: Jurors in O.J. Simpson's civil trial did something on Wednesday that the jury in his 1995 criminal case failed to do -- they deliberated for a full day without reaching a verdict.

The panel of seven women and five men, who are deciding whether Simpson was responsible for the murders of his ex-wife and her friend, wrapped up six hours of closed-door meetings before leaving court for the day, a court spokeswoman said.
It took jurors in the criminal trial less than four hours to acquit the former football star in the murders of his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman.
But jurors in the civil wrongful-death suit have already deliberated more than eight hours since the judge turned the case over to them on Tuesday.
Confined to a cramped, windowless room inside the Santa Monica courthouse, the panellists gave little hint of where they were heading in their deliberations.

They communicated only once with the judge, asking him for the kind of small magnifying glass used to examine photographs and for a picture of a test tube similar to one that was used to store a sample of Simpson's blood.
